title: Stacks, Queues and Deques
summary: The restricted containers - stacks (last in, first out) for undo, matching brackets and evaluating expressions, queues (first in, first out) built as ring buffers, deques open at both ends, the standard adapters std::stack, std::queue and std::deque, and the monotonic-deque trick for sliding-window maximums.

cards.q: Which structure suits an undo feature?
cards.a:
A stack: the most recent action is undone first

Undo reverses actions newest first, which is LIFO.

cards.q: Why is a std::vector a poor queue?
cards.a:
Removing from the front shifts every remaining element, O(n)

A ring buffer or deque removes from the front in O(1).

cards.q: A ring buffer of capacity 8 has head = 6 and size = 4. Which slot does the next push write to?
cards.a:
2

(6 + 4) % 8 = 2: the queue occupies slots 6, 7, 0, 1, so the next free slot is 2.
